title: Provenance schema: required verified object (subject_digest/as_of/recorded_at), PROV-O vocabulary
description: ODOC-231 Decision SS5-6. verified becomes a required object, never a bare date: subject_digest (required - the exact bytes measured), as_of (required - when the claim was last known true), recorded_at (required - when the assertion was authored), stale_after (optional - recheck boundary), subject_name (optional, non-authoritative label). Absent stale_after means UNKNOWN, never FRESH. A re-verification is a NEW record pointing at the old digest, never an edit to the old verified: field in place (OCI referrers pattern) - editing in place destroys verification history. Add PROV-O vocabulary (derived_from, revision_of, specialization_of, generated_at, invalidated_at) as short frontmatter names inside the EXISTING relations axis - do not open a second relation axis - each bound to its PROV IRI in one machine-readable schema table. Each document names the schema it was authored against and that name is never rewritten; use FULL_TRANSITIVE compatibility (this corpus is a permanent archive); never add a required field going forward, only optional-with-default, enforcing required-ness as a lint on new documents rather than a schema constraint, so history is never invalidated. Guard per Decision SS6: version identity (the new content-addressed blob SHA from LCLI-547) is a fourth independent axis alongside lifecycle status/delivery rollup/claim state (ADR-0019/0021) and must NOT be derived from or feed claim_version - a hash changing on a typo fix must not flag every dependent for review.

acceptanceCriteria.text: verified carries subject_digest, as_of and recorded_at, with stale_after and subject_name optional, and absent stale_after read as UNKNOWN not FRESH -- their required-ness enforced by the authoring lint of AC[4], NOT as a JSON Schema required constraint on the existing corpus. Check this against the lint and the schema together; checking it against the schema alone can pass while violating AC[4].
A re-verification creates a new record referencing the prior digest rather than editing verified: in place
derived_from/revision_of/specialization_of/generated_at/invalidated_at exist inside the existing relations axis (no second axis), each mapped to its PROV IRI in one schema table
Schema evolution never adds a required field to existing documents; new required-ness is enforced as a lint on newly authored docs only
claim_version remains author-declared and is never derived from the new content-addressed revision identity

The fate of the existing required `by` field is decided and stated -- kept, moved into the new object, or dropped -- and if dropped, the removal is handled as a compatibility event on a permanent archive rather than a schema edit

The migration is specified against the MEASURED before-state (stale_after as a top-level sibling; verified as anyOf {by,at} with additionalProperties open), not as a greenfield add; documents carrying extra keys under the open additionalProperties are accounted for

implementationNotes: BEFORE-STATE MEASURED 2026-09-20, after opum-cli-e2e pointed out this is a move plus a rename plus additions rather than a greenfield add. Verified in this repo's committed .lore/schemas: stale_after ALREADY ships as a TOP-LEVEL SIBLING property (not inside verified) in 8 schemas -- adr, arc, attested-computation, epic, reference, runbook, spec, story. opum-cli-e2e counted 7 in their bundle, which is correct for them: the 8th is arc.schema.json from LCLI-554's unreleased Arc rename. verified today is an anyOf of {by, at} -- BOTH required, additionalProperties OPEN -- or an array of the same. subject_digest appears in no schema. So today's single 'at' is exactly the as_of/recorded_at conflation ODOC-231 SS5 designs out, and the open additionalProperties means real documents may already carry keys this task has not surveyed. TWO GAPS THIS EXPOSED. (1) 'by' appeared ZERO times in this task's description and criteria, yet it is a REQUIRED field of verified in all 8 schemas and is absent from ODOC-231 SS5's field list -- now AC[6]. (2) AC[1] as originally written ('verified is a required object with required subject_digest, as_of, recorded_at') reads as a JSON Schema constraint and could be checked green against a schema that violates AC[4]'s 'never adds a required field to existing documents'; AC[1] is reworded to name the lint as the enforcement point. opum-cli-e2e has offered to pin the before-state in their suite so the transition is measurable from both sides; accepted.

THE 'by' FORK IS SHARPER THAN 'is it kept', raised by opum-cli-e2e 2026-09-20 and recorded as theirs. 'by' is not merely required, it carries a PATTERN: ^(?:[^\s/:]+\/[^\s/]+|human:\S+|process:\S+)$ -- so it encodes an ACTOR VOCABULARY (org/repo, human:, process:) and not just a string. None of ODOC-231 SS5's five fields replaces it: subject_digest names the bytes measured, as_of and recorded_at name two times, subject_name is explicitly non-authoritative. NOTHING IN THE NEW LIST SAYS WHO. So both arms of the fork are consequential rather than one being obvious: drop 'by' and the actor vocabulary goes with it, from a permanent archive; keep it and SS5's field table is incomplete rather than the schema being wrong. THIS IS A QUESTION FOR THE ADR'S OWNER (opum-agent, recorded in opum-doc), not one the implementation should settle by picking whichever is easier to build -- an implementer meeting AC[6] should route it rather than decide it. Note it is the same question as the AC[1]/AC[4] tension seen from the other side: a field cannot be required by AC[1] and forbidden by AC[4] unless the requiredness lives in the authoring lint, which AC[1] now says in its own text rather than leaving derivable.
